review_notes: I read the whole file. I also grepped the repo for uses of projectString and the embed lemmas, and compared them with the parallel LengthRestriction.lean, which defines projectString as an abbrev and has projectString_append. The file has no @[simp] attributes at all. I found two issues: a projectString interface that simp cannot see through, and small normalisation lemmas used only by rw. Nothing was run in Lean, so the suggested replacements are untested. I did not find any simp loops or competing rules, since no rules are tagged.

findings.excerpt: def projectString (u : List (Symbol T (N ⊕ T))) : List (Symbol T N) := u.map projectSymbol
findings.problem: projectString is a plain def, while its siblings embedString and rightEmbedString are abbrevs. The standard List.map lemmas (map_append, map_cons, map_nil) therefore cannot fire on it, and the file has no projectString_append or projectString_cons lemma. Every proof has to unfold it first with `unfold projectString`, `simp only [projectString, ...]` or `rw [..., projectString]`. See the unfolds at lines 223 and 231 in restrictTerminals_produces_derives_projectString and at line 325 in restrictTerminals_correct. The same file also has `simp only [projectString, projectSymbol, List.map_cons, List.map_nil]` at line 186. The unfold exposes List.map, which is only a partial normal form: it leaves projectSymbol applied to terms, so the `projectSymbol_nonterminal` rewrite at line 326 is still needed afterwards. The sibling file LengthRestriction.lean already took the other route, with an abbrev projectString and an explicit projectString_append.
findings.proposed_change: Make projectString an `abbrev`, as embedString and rightEmbedString are. Alternatively, keep the def and add `@[simp] lemma projectString_append`, `projectString_cons` and `projectString_nil`, plus `@[simp] projectSymbol_nonterminal_inl` and `projectSymbol_terminal`. Then the `unfold projectString; repeat rw [List.map_append]` steps in restrictTerminals_produces_derives_projectString can become `simp only [projectString_append]` or a plain `simp`. The final chain in restrictTerminals_correct can also shrink.
findings.benefit: Proofs about project/embed strings reduce with simp to a canonical list-map form without manual unfolding. This makes the file consistent with embedString and rightEmbedString, and with the parallel LengthRestriction file. Downstream proofs also become shorter and less fragile.

findings.excerpt:
lemma projectString_rightEmbedString_id {u : List (Symbol T N)} :
    projectString (rightEmbedString u) = u := by
findings.problem: These lemmas are all oriented as canonical simplifications. Each rewrites a compound expression to a smaller one: project∘rightEmbed = id, project of an inl nonterminal, project or embed of a terminal map, and embed of an append. None is tagged @[simp], and they are applied only by explicit `rw`, as at lines 188, 318, 324 and 326. The consumers therefore follow each lemma with hand-written clean-up. For example, restrictTerminals_correct does `rw [projectString_terminals] at hw'`, then `unfold projectString`, then `rwa [List.map_cons, List.map_nil, projectSymbol_nonterminal]`. Because the identities are not in the simp set, the normal form of embed/project expressions is not available to simp.
findings.proposed_change: Mark the terminating, directed lemmas @[simp]: projectString_rightEmbedString_id, projectSymbol_nonterminal, projectString_terminals, embedString_terminals, and, if embedString is kept as a def, embedString_append. Together with the projectString interface change in the previous finding, restrictTerminals_correct and restrictTerminalRule_left could then close their bookkeeping with `simpa using ...`. embedString_append is already List.map_append by rfl, so it needs no new attribute while embedString stays an abbrev. Note that projectString_terminals and embedString_terminals have LHSs of the form `List.map Symbol.terminal` under a projection, so there is no overlap with List.map_map.
findings.benefit: Callers stop repeating project/embed bookkeeping. The simp normal form of embed and project expressions becomes canonical, and each rule has a clear non-looping orientation.
